evidence: The survivor uses “2-colouring” and treats the graph as “0 = left, 1 = right”; the statement explicitly says links run between the two categories.
affordance_in_statement: In this system the devices split into **two categories**, and **every interference link connects a device in one category to a device in the other** — there is no interference between two devices of the same category. (The categories are not given to you; you may recover them from the links.)
removal_suggestion: There is no safe rewording that removes this affordance while preserving the intended efficient exact problem: the two-category promise is the core structural restriction. To defeat the survivor, remove the promise that all links cross two categories, but this changes the problem into general Independent Set and loses the stated tractability.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: BFS/DFS two-colors the guaranteed bipartite graph, then constructs an independent group from bipartition sides, taking advantage of the fact that vertices on one side have no internal links.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The devices split into two categories, and every interference link connects a device in one category to a device in the other.

common_affordance: the guarantee that the interference graph is bipartite with a recoverable two-category partition

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The code keeps global group lists while starting separate BFS components, so the arbitrary color orientation of disconnected components is not handled reliably; a globally accumulated color class need not represent one valid actual category and can miss the optimal combination of component sides.

Its component-based approach is vulnerable to combining or selecting component partitions incorrectly rather than accounting for the independently orientable sides of every connected component when forming an exact-size group.

It initializes `color` with zero but also uses zero as a valid color, so `if color[start] == 0` cannot distinguish an unvisited vertex from a vertex already assigned to color zero; component traversal is therefore incorrect.

recommended_edit: Remove or substantially weaken the sentence guaranteeing that every link crosses one of two categories, replacing it with an unrestricted interference-link graph. This is the only single edit that attacks the structural shortcut used by the survivor, although it changes the computational nature of the task.
regression_risk: Removing the bipartite promise would also invalidate the intended efficient solution and may make the task computationally intractable; no wording-only edit can safely defeat this survivor while retaining the same problem.
